entries.title: Genesis 23:1
segments: The longest like must come to an end, the dearest connections be sundered, and the most intimate friends part to meet no more on earth.

entries.title: Genesis 23:3
segments: Heth; the son of Canaan, and grandson of Ham.  His descendants were called Hittites.

entries.title: Genesis 23:4
segments: The bodies of those we most love must soon be buried out of our sight.

entries.title: Genesis 23:6
segments: In the choice of our sepulchres; the proposal of the Hittites was generous, but it did not meet the wishes of Abraham.  He was unwilling to bury Sarah in any sepulchre of the Canaanites, choosing rather to have a burying-place which would be exclusively his own.

entries.title: Genesis 23:9
segments: Machpelah; a tract of land owned by Ephron, in which was a cave.
A burial-place, as a memento of the evil of sin, should lead us to abhor sin, and by believing in Him who is "the resurrection and the life," to obtain deliverance from its power.

entries.title: Genesis 23:12
segments: True politeness, and a courteous, gentlemanly demeanor are the indispensable duty of all, especially of the friends of God; and the more distinguished men are, the greater is the importance of their being patterns of discretion, propriety, and good manners.

entries.title: Genesis 23:15
segments: Four hundred shekels; about two hundred dollars.

entries.title: Genesis 23:16
segments:
Weighed--the silver; to determine its value, as was the custom in those days, there being no coined money. 
 
  Current money with the merchant; in respect to both weight and quality. 
 
Perfect honesty in making bargains, and strict punctuality in fulfilling them, are duties sacredly binding upon all; and those who do not thus act, violate the first principles not only of morality, but of religion.

entries.title: Genesis 23:20
segments: All conveyances of property from one person to another should, at the time, be made sure, and thus occasion of contention be prevented.
